Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear summary. We can do the seat-level carve-out and support netting, and we have two common patterns depending on your AP workflow:

- Option A: One master invoice with separate allocation lines (legal entity tags per line). Good for a single payment run; requires your AP to accept an allocation CSV.
- Option B: Separate invoices per legal entity with an offsetting credit note applied to the entity that holds the pre-paid credit. This is cleaner for bookkeeping if each entity posts invoices separately.

For VAT: if AstraNova EU will be the billed entity we need the EU VAT ID and an invoice address for the Luxembourg entity to apply reverse charge (if appropriate). For now I'll prepare a draft using Option A and include a seat_allocation_matrix template for you to populate.

Next steps from our side:
- I will loop in Revenue Ops and Billing to confirm netting mechanics.
- I will attach a draft split invoice and the CSV template.

Can you confirm which AP workflow you prefer (single master invoice + CSV vs separate invoices)? If separate invoices, please also confirm billing contact and VAT ID for the EU entity.

Thanks,

Monica / Connor — my take after reviewing AstraNova's note and our billing policy:

1) Accounting recommendation
- Option B (separate invoices per legal entity) is the safer audit trail when the customer posts to different general ledgers. It avoids cross-entity revenue recognition complexity.
- However, Option A (master invoice + allocation CSV) is acceptable if AstraNova's AP can accept and post allocations; it reduces docs but requires careful tagging.

2) Netting/credits
- For the $12k pre-paid credit, issue a credit note referencing the original invoice, then apply an offset to the invoices for the entity that holds the credit. We should NOT post an internally-allocated negative line that transfers credit between legal entities without a corresponding credit note — that complicates intercompany reconciliation.

3) Implementation details (billing ops)
- We'll produce separate PDFs per entity and include a consolidated allocation CSV that maps invoice_line_id -> entity_tax_id -> cost_center_code.
- For non-US (EU) VAT: include a VAT field on the CSV and a tax_type column; Redwood can leave VAT amount blank until we receive the EU VAT ID, then reissue the invoice with reverse charge notation if applicable.

I've attached a sample seat_allocation_matrix (fills rows: seat_email, cost_center, entity, amount). I'll prepare the credit note template and a one-page redline on how we map invoice lines to entity tax ids.

Ben
Senior Billing Manager
Redwood Inference
